WHAT CHANGED IN v61 -- A WITH-STATEMENT INTERFACE PREFIX LIVES EXACTLY AS LONG AS ITS STATEMENT
  Two shipped defects, one cause, and both fired only when the with statement was NOT the first statement
  of its begin..end block.  tblocknode.simplify merges a strippable block into the enclosing statement
  list when that block is not the first statement there (the merge looks one statement ahead).  The
  hidden statement list a with statement is built from (internalstatements: prefix temp create, its
  assignment, the body, the temp deletes) is such a block.  Since v59 numbers and releases interface temps
  per source statement, every spliced piece became a source statement of its own:
    * "with Make.o do begin ... end"  (Make returns a COM interface, .o is the raw object inside it): the
      assignment piece released the interface BEFORE the body ran, so the body worked on a freed object.
      In v59 AND v60, x86_64-linux and win64, -O- and -O2.  This is the defect v61 exists for.
    * "with Make do begin ... end": the prefix temps were deleted under statement marks newer than their
      own stamp and leaked until routine exit (v59).  GOD's 407ef9bb3a closed this half in v60; it stays.
  v61 never merges a compiler-built list into a source block.  A nested begin..end is a source block
  itself and may still be merged: its statements are real ones.  Measured consequence: nothing is
  released earlier than the end of the with statement, nothing later, and a temp made INSIDE the body is
  still released at the end of its own statement.

  What does NOT change: everything v59 promised (a function-result interface temp dies with its
  statement; stored interfaces live as long as they always did; escapes are swept at routine exit).

  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change, so every existing unit
  set stays valid: win64 units are STILL the v52 set, linux64 units are STILL the v59 set.

PLATFORMS STILL AT v59 (NOT rebuilt for this cut) -- AND WHAT THAT MEANS
  aarch64-linux, arm-linux, arm-linux-cross, i386-linux-cross, x86_64-darwin, aarch64-darwin.
  The defect above is target-independent codegen, so the published v59 compilers for these six targets
  HAVE it.  They were left at v59 because none has a consumer today (darwin has never executed a program,
  armhf has never run on hardware, aarch64 ran once as a verification on Gray's box), the order that
  produced v60 and v61 named Windows, and a cross cut is not a five-minute job (RELEASE-v59.txt names the
  qemu/loadcheck/truncation gates each one needs).  A v61 cut for any of them is one recipe run; say which.

HOW THE DEFECT WAS FOUND (cycle 1168, evidence under ~/src/vibepascal-slices/v60-3c-cy1168/)
  * Bruno's sixteen with-prefix corners for the v60 cut compile to byte-identical code on v59 and v60 (the
    only assembly difference is the version string), so they never touched the changed path.
  * A Delphi-style matrix (generic IHolder<T>, inline vars, raw .o) found nine corners v59 leaks and v60
    releases -- every one a with that is NOT the first statement of its block.
  * A throwaway compiler that prints every temp's stamp, every statement mark and every release decision
    showed the with's hidden statement list numbered as separate statements from the second statement of
    a block on, and the merge site in tblocknode.simplify confirmed it (forinline is true in pass_1, so it
    happens at every optimisation level).
  * The same trace predicted the raw-pointer early release; a second matrix measured it on v59, on v60,
    on the v60 linux build and on the exact published v60 win64 exe under wine64.

HONEST LIMITS
  1. wine is not Windows.  GOD's UT_HolderVerbose (and, if it exists, a 3b-shaped test that is not the
     first statement of its routine) on real Windows is the sign-off for v61 as it was for v60.
  2. Six targets stay at v59 with the defect, by the reasoning above.
  3. The corpus A/B scores compile status and run exit code per test, not object lifetimes; the lifetime
     programs (tintfwithprefix1, tintfstmttemp1/2, tintflifetime1) are the lifetime gate.

ADDENDUM 2026-09-22 (cycle 1169) -- SUPERSEDED FOR BOTH TARGETS BY v62; NOTHING ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN
  Every digest and every measurement above still describes the v61 bytes exactly as published; they remain
  in dist/ and remain fetchable.  What changed is that v61 was found to carry an OLDER, unrelated defect
  that v62 fixes: a unit compiled from source is "reloaded" rather than recompiled when a unit it resolved
  symbols out of is reset mid-build, so an incremental Lazarus IDE build dies with EAccessViolation (exit
  217) in tderef.build under writeppu.  Measured on the exact published v61 binaries, and on v60 and v59
  too -- it arrived with the ctask scheduler, not with the with-statement work above.  The win64 pointer
  dist/win64/LATEST.txt now serves v62; see dist/RELEASE-v62.txt.  The with-statement lifetime fix this
  file records is unchanged and is carried forward in v62.
